extracted.intended_audience: government communicators (members of the Government Communication Service), communications leaders in UK departments, agencies and ALBs
extracted.subtask_description: A UK government-wide strategy setting standards, operating models, and commitments for public sector communications across departments, agencies and arm's length bodies, covering collaboration, digital transformation, people, trust and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak with one voice / cross-government communications plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a central strategy and planning function in GCS to develop and support delivery of an annual communications plan and make sure Ministers have clear visibility of campaign delivery and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build on use of insight and evaluation to replicate pandemic approach for other priorities; ensure campaigns support cross-government objectives, join-up with other departments and support stronger government brands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spending controls and audience-focussed expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use spending controls to challenge expenditure which does not demonstrate an audience-focussed approach, support cross-government objectives, join-up with other departments, support stronger government brands, or show that low cost routes have been fully explored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expenditure should be justified by audience focus and joined-up impact; low-cost alternatives must be considered before paid-for campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central GCS operating model — focus and sustainable funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Restructure and reduce the size of the central team and introduce a new and more sustainable funding model so the central GCS team focuses on strategy and coordination of cross-government communications; setting and assuring standards; and providing expert and shared services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central team should do only activities that it alone can do to support collaboration and joined-up work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stronger networks, external oversight and challenging orthodoxies
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a new GCS external advisory board to make recommendations on strategy and scrutinise campaign value for money and effectiveness; leverage external supplier relationships and use 'red teams' of internal and external experts to challenge conventional thinking and consider radical alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Building alliances with the private sector and using external scrutiny is recommended to achieve goals more quickly and test assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis planning and coordinated response
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring crisis comms capabilities into a central strategy and planning function responsible for crisis plans, horizon scanning, crisis response coordination, and crisis reviews so government can work together speaking with one voice during a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaboration and a single plan are emphasised as most important during crises to ensure consistent messaging and coordinated action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital communications standards, quality and capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a central digital comms strategy and model of best practice led by an enhanced digital communications hub to drive up quality and consistency of digital products; update functional standards to ensure the role of a modern digital team is fully reflected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data analysis and visualisation must be core competencies; every department should have broadcast expertise and GCS should attract experienced broadcast specialists to raise capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of data, personalisation and innovation (AI and speech tech)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications campaigns should increasingly use data to deliver an individual experience (personalisation) with less reliance on mass communication; publish a GCS innovation strategy and consider insight, data, applied AI and speech technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a virtual GCS Innovation Lab to identify, develop, test, execute and scale system-changing innovation and publish a GCS Data Strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency, data-driven planning and cost reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a regular data reporting and business planning cycle to challenge departments on how they are driving efficiency and reducing headcount; use data to support departments and ALBs to drive efficiencies through functional standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central team to lead by example with a smaller stronger structure; reduce government spending on paid marketing by encouraging low-cost techniques and joining-up campaigns; identify opportunities to rationalise commercial contracts to deliver economies of scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining public trust and countering misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Work alongside international partners to take action against misinformation and disinformation, and take a systematic, evidence-based approach to build societal and individual resilience while taking responsibility for our own content and behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce mandatory training on GCS propriety guidance, clarify how members can raise concerns, publish a paper on AI ethics in digital marketing, and review/revise propriety guidance on application of new technology (privacy, non-discrimination, fairness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional accreditation and functional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a professional accreditation and qualification model and assess all communicators against it to ensure people are operating at the expected standard; update the communications functional standard to detail knowledge, skills and attributes required by discipline and level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit current skills and future needs; work with Government Skills and Curriculum Unit and external partners to create a stronger curriculum and an online learning system to assess capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skills audit and capability development (data & broadcast focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit the skills GCS currently has and those needed for the future, recognising that data analysis, visualisation and broadcast capability are in short supply and should be developed across departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every department should have broadcast expertise; attract experienced broadcast specialists; make data analysis and visualisation core competencies for communicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talent attraction, entry routes and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Build an inspiring brand and a talent attraction strategy highlighting unique opportunities in GCS; review talent programmes to identify future leaders; continue apprenticeships and internships; develop new entry routes for people from business, third sector and public service rotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for GCS to be a destination of choice; ensure a diverse external early talent pipeline and new temporary or secondment routes into government communication roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership expectations and capability framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Set clear expectations of senior leaders, launch a new leadership capability framework, identify and invest in key skills development for leaders, and refresh the heads of discipline model so each communications discipline has clear leadership and responsibility for driving improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide targeted development to keep leaders up to date with latest technology and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusion in recruitment and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase ambition of the diversity and inclusion action plan with realistic commitments, improve the quality of diversity data collected, and ensure government communications campaigns reflect and reach a diverse range of audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity of thought and representation is framed as critical to operational effectiveness and to communicating effectively across the UK.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic distribution and GCS careers outside London
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a GCS location strategy with a target for the number of GCS roles in Whitehall departments to be based outside London by 2025, and create GCS hubs where communicators can develop careers and work across departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address current London concentration (81% of roles) to widen the talent pool and better reflect citizens' views across the UK.
